R-squared variance-budget prior for formula terms

Source: R/priors-R2.R
prior_R2.Rd

Declares a joint prior distribution for the coefficients of several formula terms through a budget for the explained variance. The total R-squared of the terms has the Beta prior total, its signal-to-noise ratio \(W = r / (1 - r)\) is allocated to the terms by the Dirichlet prior allocation, and each term turns its share into coefficients by the selected coefficient law. Place the object in a formula prior list under a name that is not a formula term, which names the budget (e.g., R2 = prior_R2(...)); see Details.

prior_R2(
  terms = NULL,
  total = prior("beta", list(1, 1)),
  allocation = R2_dirichlet(),
  inclusion = NULL,
  model = R2_model()
)

Arguments

terms

character vector of the formula term labels of the budget in the full candidate model (e.g., c("x", "f", "x:f"); "x:f" and "f:x" name the same term), or NULL (default) for every fixed-effect term of the formula that has no prior of its own and that no other budget names (at most one budget of a formula; a term with a point prior at zero stays in it, excluded from the model). Terms of the budget that a model's formula does not contain are deleted, and the budget is redistributed in full to the retained terms.

total

Beta prior on the total R-squared of the full candidate model, prior("beta", list(alpha = a, beta = b)) (default Beta(1, 1)), or a spike-and-slab prior with that Beta slab, prior_spike_and_slab(prior("beta", ...), prior_inclusion = ...), whose spike is zero signal in the budget (the budget null) and whose inclusion prior is a probability prior (prior("spike", list(p)) or a Beta prior). Other mixtures are not supported.

allocation

Dirichlet allocation of the budget of the full candidate model to its terms, from R2_dirichlet() (default flat: concentration 1 for every term). A budget of one term has the single concentration of its term, which the linked convention and the kernel laws use.

inclusion

inclusion gates of the terms, which make one fit average over the models of the budget: NULL (default) for no gates; one probability prior for every term, prior("spike", list(p)) for a common fixed inclusion probability or prior("beta", list(a, b)) for a shared inclusion rate (a beta-binomial prior over the models); or a list of probability priors named by term labels for independent gates of the listed terms (the other terms are always included). A Beta prior in the list is marginally its mean probability for its term; a shared rate needs the single-prior form.

model

the fixed model choices of the budget, from R2_model(): the coefficient law, the cross-model convention and concentration, the residual scale sigma and the factor contrast (defaults: exact law, common convention, inherited concentrations, "sigma", orthonormal contrasts).

Value

prior_R2 returns an object of class "BayesTools_R2_budget".

Details

R-squared budgets are a beta feature for BayesTools formulas. The residual SD scales each term's contribution to the linear predictor. Its fitted coefficients are expressed in residual-SD units.

A formula prior list declares a budget with an entry such as R2 = prior_R2(...). The name of the entry names the budget: the total R-squared is the formula parameter <parameter>_<name> (displayed as <name>{total}), and the share of the budget allocated to a retained term is displayed as <name>[share: <term>]; both are quantities of parameter_catalog() that the estimates tables show and hypothesis_BF() tests (e.g., "R2{total} > 0.1" or "R2[share: f] > 0.5"), with the Beta prior of the total in the model and the Beta marginal of the share under the allocation. The name must be a valid JAGS node name that contains no "intercept", does not end in a suffix of the nodes that BayesTools generates ("_ordered", "_indicator", "_inclusion", "_variable", "_allocation", "_gate", "_open", "_rate", "_rate_u"), and neither it nor the names of its nodes is a term label. Several budgets are several entries (for example, a budget for compulsory covariates and a separate budget for the tested terms, whose R-squared is then the incremental partial R-squared of the tested terms when their design blocks are orthogonal to the covariates; with correlated blocks it is the share of the tested terms' own signal variance, not their partial R-squared). Every term of a budget must not have its own prior in the list, except a point prior at zero (prior("spike", list(0)) or prior_none()), which excludes it from the model and from the budget. Terms that no budget names keep their own priors.

total and allocation describe the full candidate model. In a model \(M\) with retained allocation units \(u\) (the terms for law = "exact", the coded coefficients for the kernels, each with its term's concentration) the prior is $$r \sim \textrm{Beta}(a_M, b_M), \quad W = r / (1 - r), \quad \phi \sim \textrm{Dirichlet}(\alpha_M),$$ with \((a_M, b_M)\) given by the convention and \(\alpha_M\) by the concentration of model. With convention = "linked", the first shape of total must equal the total concentration \(A\) of the full model (the default total is not changed: the error names the required total): the sum of the concentrations of allocation for the exact law or with concentration = "fixed_total", and the sum of the concentrations times the numbers of coded coefficients of the terms for the kernels with inherited concentrations (checked when JAGS_formula() binds the budget, which then needs the data of all terms of the budget).

With the centered design block \(X_t\) of a term and its empirical metric \(G_t = X_t^\top C X_t / n\), the coefficients in residual-SD units are

  • "exact": \(\beta_t = \sqrt{W \phi_t}\, R_t^{-1} u_t\), with \(R_t^\top R_t = G_t\) and \(u_t\) uniform on the unit sphere, so the term's signal variance \(\beta_t^\top G_t \beta_t\) equals \(W \phi_t\) for every draw and the law of its fitted contribution does not depend on the contrast;

  • "normal": \(\beta_j \sim N(0, W \phi_j / G_{t,jj})\);

  • "laplace": \(\beta_j \sim \textrm{Laplace}(0, \sqrt{W \phi_j / (2 G_{t,jj})})\).

When the term blocks are mutually orthogonal, the realized R-squared of the budget equals \(r\) for every draw under "exact". With correlated terms, the signal variance of the whole budget differs from \(W\) by the cross products of the terms' contributions. A model with a single retained unit has \(\phi = 1\); a model whose budget retains no term has no signal from it.

The prior targets the empirical variance of the fitted contributions, computed with denominator \(n\) in the fitted data; unequal cell counts therefore weight the levels of a factor by their frequencies. With treatment contrasts, the intercept prior applies to the reference level rather than to the grand mean.

A budget without terms takes the terms of each formula it binds to, so that formula is its full candidate model. This is what a single fit with inclusion gates needs; models of a model space fitted separately under the "linked" or "conditioning" convention or with concentration = "fixed_total" need explicit terms naming the full model, because without them each fit is its own full model. Random-effect terms are never part of a budget without terms.

The R2 term priors that JAGS_formula() binds support the prior methods (rng(), mpdf(), mcdf(), mquant(), mean(), var(), plot()) of single coefficients, and of factor levels under the exact law, by deterministic quadrature over the budget. The levels of a factor term are also catalog quantities (parameter_catalog()) with the prior law of each level (any level under the exact law, also with unequal cell counts; single coded coefficients under the kernels), which parameter_prior_density() and hypothesis_BF() use. On the original scale of declared predictor scales (transform_scaled = TRUE), a coefficient that the scale transformation multiplies by a constant has its rescaled law. The prior densities of combinations of several parameters of one budget (an original-scale coefficient that combines several fitted coefficients among them), ordinates at a point (Savage-Dickey ratios and point hypotheses of coefficients) and the common level marginal of the term methods for the kernels with three or more levels or for unequal marginals are unavailable; point hypotheses at a bound of the support of a share, a total or an inclusion rate are refused (the posterior density of the draws has no exact ordinate there).

With inclusion gates or a spike-and-slab total, one fit averages over the models of the budget. A configuration \(S\) of open terms (the open gated terms and the ungated terms) is a model, and given \(S\) the coefficients follow exactly the prior of model \(S\) as a separate fit under the same convention, concentration and law: the allocation is redistributed over the open terms (a gate of a kernel term closes all its coded coefficients), the total is Beta(a, b) ("common"), Beta(\(A_S\), b) ("linked", sampled as term signals \(g_t G_t / H\) with \(G_t\) Gamma(\(\alpha_t\)) and \(H\) Gamma(b)) or Beta(\(a - (A - A_S)\), \(b + (A - A_S)\)) ("conditioning"), and "fixed_total" rescales the concentrations of the open units. The model \(S\) is the formula of the fit with the closed terms excluded, as a point prior at zero excludes them: the coded columns of the open terms do not change. A closed main effect therefore leaves its interactions coded as in the full formula (in ~ f * x with x closed, f:x keeps its coded columns of the full formula, not the slopes in every level of f of a refit of ~ f + f:x). With gates only, the empty configuration is the budget null, with prior probability \(\prod_t (1 - \pi_t)\) (or its beta-binomial value). A spike-and-slab total makes the null its own event with the spike weight \(\pi_0\): when every term is gated, the gate prior under the slab is conditioned on a nonempty configuration, \(P(S) = (1 - \pi_0) \pi(S) / (1 - \pi(\emptyset))\); with an ungated term no conditioning is needed. The gates are sampled exactly as a sequence of Bernoulli nodes, each with its probability given the gates before it, so the number of gated terms is not limited. The realized total is zero under the null. The prior methods of the term priors (rng(), mcdf(), mquant(), mean(), var(), plot()) include the atom at zero of a closed term (mpdf() is the density of the continuous part), and those of the total entry the atom at zero of the budget null. These prior laws sum over the gate configurations through their open concentrations, exactly and without a limit on the number of gated terms (the configurations are aggregated into at most 65536 distinct states, which few distinct concentrations keep small). A shared Beta(a, b) inclusion rate \(\theta\) is the node <parameter>_<name>_rate and the catalog quantity <name>{inclusion rate}, drawn given the gates as \(\theta | S \sim\) Beta(\(a + s\), \(b + K - s\)) with \(s\) of the \(K\) gates open (without changing the sampler of the gates); its prior is Beta(a, b), or, when the gate prior is conditioned on a nonempty configuration, the law of \(\theta\) given that condition. Condition events over several terms (and the total) of one gated budget, as in as_mixed_posteriors(conditional = ...), use their exact joint prior law. The point mass at zero of a gated coefficient or a total is the exclusion of its term or the null of the budget, tested by the inclusion Bayes factors of runjags_inference_table() (or, for a total, the region hypothesis "<name>\{total\} > 0"); the atom at one of a share (its term is the only open term) is tested by region hypotheses such as "<name>[share: x] >= 1". Bridge sampling of a gated or spiked budget is unavailable (the fit is itself the model average) and stops with BayesTools_R2_gated_unavailable.

Conditions

Invalid budgets and bindings stop with BayesTools_R2_invalid; unavailable results with BayesTools_R2_unavailable (with BayesTools_R2_unbound for a term prior used before JAGS_formula() binds it, and BayesTools_R2_density_unavailable for an implied distribution); a coefficient state outside the support of the budget with BayesTools_R2_invalid_state (also BayesTools_marglik_out_of_support). All inherit BayesTools_R2_condition. Linear combinations of several parameters of one budget stop with BayesTools_formula_measure_unavailable.

See also

R2_model(), R2_dirichlet(), JAGS_formula(), prior_factor()

Examples

# the defaults: every term of the formula without its own prior, a
# uniform total R-squared, a flat allocation, exact allocation
prior_R2()
#> R-squared budget prior (exact allocation)
#>   terms:      every formula term without its own prior (resolved when the formula binds the budget)
#>   total:      Beta(1, 1) in every model
#>   allocation: flat Dirichlet, retained terms keep their concentrations
#>   scale:      coefficients in units of 'sigma'
#>   contrast:   orthonormal (factor terms only)

budget <- prior_R2(
  terms      = c("x", "f"),
  total      = prior("beta", list(alpha = 1, beta = 1)),
  allocation = R2_dirichlet(c(x = 1, f = 2)),
  model      = R2_model(law = "exact", convention = "common")
)
budget
#> R-squared budget prior (exact allocation)
#>   terms:      x, f
#>   total:      Beta(1, 1) in every model
#>   allocation: Dirichlet(1, 2), retained terms keep their concentrations
#>   scale:      coefficients in units of 'sigma'
#>   contrast:   orthonormal (factor terms only)

# formula prior list of a model 'mu ~ x + f': the entry name 'R2' names
# the budget
formula_prior_list <- list(
  intercept = prior("normal", list(0, 10)),
  R2        = budget
)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# ANCOVA: compare the models with and without the factor f
set.seed(1)
data <- data.frame(f = factor(rep(c("a", "b", "c"), each = 20)), x = rnorm(60))
data$y <- 0.5 * (data$f == "b") + 0.3 * data$x + rnorm(60)

fit_model <- function(formula){
  arguments <- list(
    model_syntax = "model{ for(i in 1:N){ y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], 1 / pow(sigma, 2)) } }",
    data = list(y = data$y, N = nrow(data)),
    prior_list = list(sigma = prior("invgamma", list(1, 1))),
    formula_list = list(mu = formula),
    formula_data_list = list(mu = data),
    formula_prior_list = list(mu = formula_prior_list)
  )
  fit <- do.call(JAGS_fit, arguments)
  marglik <- do.call(JAGS_bridgesampling, c(list(fit = fit,
    log_posterior = function(parameters, data){
      sum(dnorm(data$y, parameters[["mu"]], parameters[["sigma"]], log = TRUE))
    }), arguments[-1]))
  list(fit = fit, marglik = marglik, prior_weights = 1)
}

# the same budget in both models: without f, x receives the whole budget
models <- models_inference(list(fit_model(~ x), fit_model(~ x + f)))
inference <- ensemble_inference(models, parameters = "mu_f",
  is_null_list = list(mu_f = c(TRUE, FALSE)), conditional = FALSE)
inference$mu_f$BF

# posterior summaries in residual-SD units, with factor levels
runjags_estimates_table(models[[2]]$fit, transform_factors = TRUE)

# implied prior distributions: the total R-squared and a coefficient
priors <- attr(models[[2]]$fit, "prior_list")
plot(priors$mu_R2)
plot(priors$mu_x)

# one fit averaging over the models of the budget: a shared inclusion rate
# (beta-binomial model prior) and a spike-and-slab total for the budget null
gated <- prior_R2(
  total     = prior_spike_and_slab(prior("beta", list(1, 1)),
                                   prior_inclusion = prior("spike", list(0.5))),
  inclusion = prior("beta", list(1, 1)),
  model     = R2_model(contrast = "meandif")
)
fit <- JAGS_fit(
  model_syntax = "model{ for(i in 1:N){ y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], 1 / pow(sigma, 2)) } }",
  data = list(y = data$y, N = nrow(data)),
  prior_list = list(sigma = prior("invgamma", list(1, 1))),
  formula_list = list(mu = ~ x + f), formula_data_list = list(mu = data),
  formula_prior_list = list(mu = list(intercept = prior("normal", list(0, 10)), R2 = gated))
)
runjags_inference_table(fit)   # inclusion of the budget and of each term
runjags_estimates_table(fit, conditional = TRUE)
} # }
